name: Turk's Cap

facts.what: Red flowers, marble-sized red fruit, young leaves
facts.how: Flowers and fruit raw or as tea; fruit cooks into syrup
facts.when: May through November, one of the longest seasons going

caution: No meaningful look-alike when flowering: nothing else here makes that never-opening red turban of a bloom. Fruit is mild and a little mealy, better cooked than grazed.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A shade-loving mallow with soft maple-ish leaves and red flowers that stay furled like a wrapped turban, hummingbird-designed.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Flowers steep into a pale hibiscus-style tea. The little red fruits taste faintly of apple and do their best work as syrup or jelly.
